what: O0 optics source diagnosis: the Target's complete glass shader byte-anchored (sites), plus runtime ROI statistics on both pages (runtime). Media differs between the pages, so runtime numbers are distribution statistics, never pixel matches.

sites.whatItSettles: The Target's glass has NO volume: one unit plane, 16x12 segments. There is no front/side/back structure, no sidewall, no back dish -- everything else is shading.
The plane is bulged onto a sphere section: z = sqrt(max(R^2-|p|^2,1)) - R with R = the LAYOUT sphere radius (uniform, written per frame). The card's curvature IS the grid sphere's curvature.
The card outline is a rounded-rectangle SDF in plane-pixel space; cornerRadius is settings.cornerRadius (0.163) x planeWidth, capped at the half extent.
opacityNode: an fwidth-antialiased cutout of the SDF. The glass NEVER paints outside the rounded rect -- zero gutter invasion is structural, not tuned.

Thickness profile: a superellipse of the SDF -- t = clamp(1 + sdf/bevelWidth, 0, 1); thickness x (1 - t^p)^(1/p) with p = bevelPower. Values: bevelWidth 0.192 x planeWidth, bevelPower 3.9, thickness 155 x cardScale. Flat centre, all the action in the bevel band.

The shading normal = sphere term (p/|sphere z|) minus the numeric thickness gradient, slope-clamped at bevelMaxSlope 1.74. One surface, one normal -- no internal fold, no return path, no second refraction event.

Refraction: eta = 1/(ior + dispersion*offset); refract the view ray at the bevel normal; travel = thickness/|r.z| (a slab-depth model); UV shift = r.xy * travel * refractStrength / planeSize. ior 2.3, refractStrength 0.7. The displacement DIVERGES toward the rim as r.z -> 0 (clamped at .05) -- that is the Target's edge compression: media squeezed by the bevel normal, inside the card's own texture.
The refracted sample is CLAMPED to the card's own media rect (cover fit) -- no scene-colour, no neighbour bleed, and at the rim the media clamps to its border pixels rather than escaping.

Spectral weights: per sample at spectral position n in [0,1], RGB weights are tent functions centred at 0 / 0.5 / 1 with half-width 0.5, normalised so each channel sums to 1 across samples. 5 samples (dispersionSamples), dispersion 0.32 spread on the IOR. The fringe is an IOR spread inside the card's own media -- NOT a screen-space RGB shift.

Reflection: mirror the view ray at the world-space normal, rotate by envRotation (-2 rad about Y) then envRotationX (0), sample the equirect environment AT LEVEL 0 -- no roughness, no blur, no PMREM. The env preset is 'studio': /hdri/studio_small_03_1k.hdr on the Target's own origin -- the white-studio reflection is a real HDR studio, not a colour.
Schlick fresnel, F0 = 0.045, exponent 5, against the BEVEL normal -- so the fresnel rises exactly where the bevel turns the normal, i.e. the white ring lives on the bevel band.

The final colour: mix(refractedMedia * tint(#fff), envReflection, min(saturate(fresnel * envIntensity 1.93), envMaxMix 0.27)) + rim. The env can replace AT MOST 27% of the media colour -- the white reflection is a capped LERP, not additive energy, so it DE-saturates the rim band toward the studio white instead of adding chroma.
Rim: smoothstep over the last rimWidth (10 x cardScale) px of the SDF, intensity 0.11, colour WHITE top and bottom (rimColor = rimColorTop = #ffffff) -- an additive white line, no hue.

toneMapped: FALSE. The card's colour -- media, reflection and rim -- reaches the framebuffer without any tone-mapping curve. Combined with the app never setting renderer.toneMapping (no such write exists in the app module; the three.js default is NoToneMapping), the Target output transform is: sRGB encode only. No ACES, no exposure, no contrast curve, no saturation stage anywhere in the chain.
The complete shipped optics parameter set. Note roughness: 0 exists as a setting but NO roughness uniform is created and no blur path exists in the material -- it is dead.
The page behind the cards: a screen-space navy (#0a1c3d) to black diagonal gradient as the scene backgroundNode.
Media textures are sRGB, clamped to edge -- the refracted sample clamp lands on repeated border pixels, which is what the edge compression squeezes against.

questions.glassGeometry: A domed unit plane -- no volume, no front/side/back split.
questions.sceneColorSampling: None. Refraction displaces UV within the card's own media texture, cover-fitted and clamped.
questions.refractionDisplacementLaw: refract(-E, bevelNormal, 1/(ior+dispersion*o)); travel = thickness/max(|r.z|,.05); uvShift = r.xy*travel*refractStrength/planeSize. Diverges toward the rim: media compression at the bevel.
questions.thicknessIor: thickness 155*cardScale over a superellipse bevel (width .192*planeW, power 3.9); ior 2.3.
questions.dispersionChannelOffsets: 5 IOR samples spread by 0.32, tent RGB weights centred 0/.5/1 width .5, channel-normalised. In-media, not screen-space.
questions.reflectionEnvironmentContribution: equirect studio_small_03_1k.hdr, level 0, rotated -2 rad Y; mixed in by min(saturate(fresnel*1.93), 0.27).
questions.roughnessBlur: NONE in the shipped shader. The roughness setting is dead.
questions.fresnelRimLaw: Schlick F0 .045 pow 5 on the bevel normal; additive white rim smoothstep over the outer 10*cardScale px, intensity .11.
questions.toneMapping: None -- material toneMapped:false, renderer left at the NoToneMapping default. sRGB encode only.
questions.outputColorSpace: Renderer default sRGB; video textures sRGB.
questions.saturationContrastPath: None exists. tint is #ffffff. Any saturation difference against our candidate comes from OUR pipeline (ACES film curve + exposure 1.05), not from a Target boost.
questions.edgeCompressionMagnification: The 1/|r.z| divergence at the bevel, clamped at .05, refractStrength .7 -- compression INTO the card's own media, clamped to its border.
questions.gutterInvasion: Structurally zero: the SDF alpha cutout ends the card at its rounded rect; rim light lives INSIDE the SDF (smoothstep of negative band).
questions.internalFoldReturnPath: None -- one refraction event on one surface.
questions.brightDarkHighTextureBehaviour: Not decidable from source alone -- runtime ROI measurement (o0 runtime half / O1 gate).

runtimeMethod.cardRects: projected AABBs from the SAME layout/culling twin on both lanes (proven slot-identical in V0), front-facing fully-on-screen cards only
runtimeMethod.chroma: max(RGB)-min(RGB); fringeRB = mean |R-B| (the cyan/magenta axis); white = min(RGB) > 180
runtimeMethod.gutter: non-card pixels between analysed cards; ink = luma > 80 over the navy-black gradient

systemGapRanking.method: measured runtime gaps (edge band statistics, media-independent by construction) attributed to the four candidate systems via the byte-anchored source differences

ranking.measuredGap: desktop edge chroma 35.91 (Target) vs 63.13 (candidate), fringe R-B axis 34.98 vs 59.46, white reflection ratio 0.204 vs 0.144 -- the candidate's edges carry ~76% more chroma and ~30% less white than the Target's
ranking.sourceCause: the Target's dispersion is an IN-MEDIA IOR spread -- 5 spectral samples, eta_i = 1/(ior + dispersion*offset_i), tent RGB weights normalised per channel (energy-conserving, chroma bounded by the media's own colours). The candidate's is a screen-space R/B tap split (dispersionUv 0.0065 both directions), which manufactures pure cyan/magenta lines at every luminance edge regardless of media content
ranking.verdict: LARGEST measured, directly on the brief's named metrics (fringe chroma, rim saturation, white reflection ratio)

ranking.measuredGap: white ratio deficit is real but co-caused by A: the chroma fringes COVER the white band. Both pages source a white studio (theirs studio_small_03_1k.hdr, fresnel-capped LERP <= 0.27)
fringe width and compression not separable from A's chroma at this round's instruments
no direct measurement; the Target has NO internal fold (single refraction event, source-read)

systemGapRanking.caveat: interior-saturation numbers compare DIFFERENT media sets (the Target shuffles its clips per load) and are indicative only; edge-band numbers are glass-dominated and carry the decision. Mobile flips fringeRB because the candidate's gutter spill (0.71 vs 0.42 ink ratio) floods the band -- recorded, not chased this round.
